# OpenCovers

> OpenCovers is an open source reservation engine for restaurants: availability, bookings, tables and a signed event feed, exposed through an HTTP API and an MCP server with 18 tools over stdio. Pre-alpha. License: Apache-2.0. Built with Node.js, Hono, Drizzle and PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL enforces the no-double-booking rule with a GiST exclusion constraint. The MCP server is the npm package `@opencovers/mcp` (`npx -y @opencovers/mcp`), also listed in the official MCP registry as `io.github.David-Cabeza/opencovers`. 74 of the 93 conformance cases pass and 9 are partial. The other 10 specify moving a booking to another date or time (C83 to C92), which is not built yet. Allergies and diets (C82) are built in the API and the staff app behind a switch that is off by default, not yet in the MCP tools.

The product around the engine: a staff app (agenda, availability, floor plan, setup; Spanish and English) and a guest booking widget for a venue's own site (in progress; seven languages, of which ca, fr, de, it and pt are machine-assisted and not yet reviewed by a native speaker; light and dark). The guest side of the public waitlist is built but off by default, with provisional wording pending legal review, and it is not enabled in the hosted demo.

Not built yet: payments and deposits, SMS and WhatsApp, reminders, reporting beyond a pacing view, POS adapters, a guest screen in the staff app and a remote MCP endpoint (only part 1, an OAuth 2.1 authorization server behind `MCP_REMOTE`, is merged, off by default). No restaurant runs on OpenCovers yet. Guest emails ship in Spanish only and their text is a placeholder pending legal review. The texts of the hosted demo (terms and privacy notice) were written without a lawyer's review. The hosted demo is a sandbox with invented data, not a service for running a real restaurant.

Goals for 2027 (these are GOALS, not facts; all three measures are zero today): a restaurant runs a full service on software it can read, host and leave, and anyone can check it works. Measures, with the goal for 15 December 2027 and the level below which we call the year a miss: venues in service, goal 10 (at least 3 run by someone other than the maintainer), miss below 3; third parties that pass the conformance kit on their own deployment, goal 3, miss below 1; outside people credited as contributors, goal 25, miss below 10. Named milestones, all goals: the Double-Booking Trial (1 March to 30 April), First Service (June, depends on a legal review and a venue) and Without the Author (third quarter, depends on a third party). A missed commitment stays on the board with its cause.

## Start here

- [Overview for developers (English)](https://opencovers.dev/en/): what it is, guarantees, API, MCP server and local setup.
- [Roadmap 2027](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): goals, measures, milestones and what is blocked on someone outside the code.
- [README](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/README.md): features, architecture and quick start.

## Contract

- [OpenAPI contract](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/docs/contract/openapi.yaml): the HTTP API under /v1.
- [MCP tools](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/docs/contract/mcp.md): the 18-tool catalog.
- [Errors](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/docs/contract/errors.md): the error vocabulary.
- [Conformance cases](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/docs/contract/conformance.md): the behavior any implementation must pass.
- [Webhooks](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/blob/main/docs/contract/webhooks.md): signed push of the event feed.

## Decisions

- [Architecture decision records](https://github.com/David-Cabeza/OpenCovers/tree/main/docs/adr): why the engine is built this way.
